1931, November
FATHER SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 1.
Page 44 Cont.
Nov. 16 To-day Mr. & Mrs. Dean (non-Cath) laments, after adopting little two-year-old, that the mother has been induced to recind her deci- sion. Now she threatens them if they refuse to give back the child. They enroll the mother, K. Hartley .... & Associates .. Co. .... W'll see.
Yesterday, Mrs. Bernandette Barker was reported as dying (child- birth) Baby born 8 o'clock night before. At 10:30 A.M. mother is enrolled. Today her husband smiles as he reports his wife having gone to sleep about same time she was enrolled - now out of danger.
Nov. 18
Mrs. Justina Nachazel 63, 15465 Fairfield Ave. dying 3 years ago with cancer of bowels; could not even take water - wonders now how she lived so long without any nourishment of any kind - thinks it was about two months. L. Ryan enrolled her for one year and she has never had any Trouble with cancer since. She wept To-day telling us about the experience - now in perfect health.
1932, January
1932 Page 45 Jan. 30 James E. Eagen 39 of Smiths Creek Michigan came 1st time January 2nd with bad tuomers of stomach or probable cancer - off and on for 13 years; this time bad since last November (about Nov. 1st) . Jan. 10th came again with wife and son - one of 8 - to enroll per- petually. To-day feels like a young man smiling and healthy - Son, Martin Eagen 19 threatened with loss of finger-top enrolls perpet- ually this a.m.
Feb. 1 Rev. H. Japes, came in 1914 to see her Niece Mrs Mary A. Stork and failing to find her he left fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00) to her cousin and wife to give to his said niece when they found her. They had frustrated his plan to see her (his niece) misinforming ing him as to her where abouts. ... After seven years her same cousin (who had frustrated the meeting of the cousins and got the $50,000.00) informed the said niece (Mrs. M. Stork) of his action in keeping the 50000. and of the visit of her Rev. Uncle. - telling her daughtter she might work for her living - We enroll them To-day - poor people. Now Mrs Stork's son and daughter - Henry J. Stork and Mrs Mary E. Whitman, refuse to accept $25.00 for settlement, the dishon- est reletive offers .. They ask to have the case enrolled in S. Mass A. They are now homeless - living with relatives. awaiting the trial to-morrow.
